title: gRNAde — RNA sequence design for a target structure
description: Design candidate RNA sequences for a target 3D structure (inverse folding). Outputs are candidates for the supplied backbone — a successful run does not validate folding or biological function.
citation: Joshi et al., gRNAde: Geometric Deep Learning for 3D RNA inverse design. https://github.com/chaitjo/geometric-rna-design

fields.name: structure
fields.label: Input structure
fields.help: One PDB file with a single RNA chain.

fields.name: chain
fields.label: RNA chain
fields.help: Auto-detected if the structure has a single RNA chain.

example_summary: A tiny synthetic 6-nucleotide RNA backbone (chain A), bundled so you can try the pipeline without hunting for a structure.
example_details: This is a hand-made placeholder fixture, not a real biological molecule: six residues (A-U-G-C-A-U) on a single RNA chain with just enough atoms to exercise parsing, chain detection, and the end-to-end run. gRNAde's job is 'inverse folding' — given a 3D backbone shape, propose RNA sequences predicted to fold into it. For this example the backbone is synthetic, so the returned sequences are only meaningful as a demonstration of the workflow. Swap in a real PDB (one RNA chain) to design for an actual target, and note that until the real model is wired in, all sequences are deterministic placeholders rather than gRNAde predictions.
notes: source_commit, checkpoint_digest, worker_image_digest, max_sequence_length and the structure max_bytes are provisional until confirmed by the M1 baseline and M4 smoke runs (see IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).
